exposure: prepregnancy maternal characteristics (e.g., age, educational attainment, employment, multiparity, chronic conditions like diabetes, hypertension, obesity, advanced maternal age, hypothyroidism)
barriers to exclusive breastfeeding (e.g., paid employment, perception of low milk production, maternal illness/medication, fatigue)
facilitators of exclusive breastfeeding (e.g., counseling from healthcare personnel)
cohort: The study included 566 women who received prenatal care and gave birth at the National Institute of Perinatology in Mexico City.
finding: The study found that prepregnancy risk conditions, multiparity, paid employment, perceived low milk production, maternal illness/medication, and fatigue were associated with an increased risk of non-exclusive breastfeeding, whereas food insecurity and counseling by healthcare personnel were protective.
followup_time: Up to 4 months (median duration of exclusive breastfeeding reported)
